headline: South Asia: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
- Asia: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Soldiers intervene on roadside to save children from alleged knife attack.
Three soldiers sprang into action when a highway crash in Washington turned into a knife attack on two children.
The Caribbean - bottom line: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
The frantic voice of her daughter pleading for help over the telephone moments before she was killed will forever haunt Natasha Hall. Hall’s daughter, 30-year-old Lashane Ellis, and her one-year-old grandson, Kaheel Daley, were killed on Friday night when armed men went to their home on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, opened fire and set the house ablaze. Before fleeing, the gunmen reportedly opened fire on a neighbouring house, killing 39-year-old Kimeisha Gibson.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Bomb disposal experts have recovered the warhead and non-explosive debris from a ballistic missile at the site of a Russian strike in the Obolonskyi district of Kyiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, just now: Russians strike two apartment blocks in Sloviansk: four injured, people may be trapped under rubble – photos, video.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian drone strikes ambulance in Sumy Oblast: driver and paramedic injured – photo.
A Russian drone struck an ambulance responding to a call in Sumy Oblast, injuring the 44-year-old driver and a 59-year-old paramedic.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.
[Dabanga] Wad El Mahi Locality / Geisan Locality / El Roseir -- Drone strikes and explosions have killed scores of civilians and injured dozens across Sudan, as attacks on displacement shelters and residential neighbourhoods in Blue Nile and North Kordofan coincide with deadly mine blasts in West Kordofan and renewed armed violence in South Darfur.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Ethiopia: UN Chief 'Gravely Concerned' By Renewed Fighting in Northern Ethiopia, Warns Against Escalation.
[UN News] UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an immediate end to the renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, saying he is deeply worried by reports that Eritrean forces are present in the country.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 12 hours ago: Niger: Niger Intelligence Agents Expelled From France in Sign of Diplomatic Strain.
[RFI] Two Nigerien intelligence officers were forced to leave France last month, French daily Le Monde has revealed, with one agent suspected of monitoring opposition figures on French soil. It is the latest sign of the deterioration in relations between the two countries since Niger's 2023 military coup.

The Board of Peace has tried to do some work on the sidelines to see what might happen after Israel’s elections. In general, the theory is that Israel won’t do anything on Gaza until afterward.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, NDTV - Top Stories, just now: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The defence pact, of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in KP as president approves cabinet decision.

- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Israeli strikes kill five in Gaza.
CAIRO: Israeli strikes killed at least five Palestinians in the Gaza Strip in two separate attacks on Saturday, health officials said. Medics said an Israeli strike killed four people near Panda Mall in Gaza City, whi­le another killed one person in the Tuffah neighbourhood further south of the city. Israel, which claims Hamas has been rea­­rming and launching attacks in violation of an October ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks. Hamas has denied trying to carry out att­a­cks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Isr­ael of undermining the Gaza peace deal.
Asia - bottom line: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, The Moscow Times, 18 hours ago: Russian attacks kill 20 in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin.
Russian strikes killed at least 20 people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, Ukrainian officials said on Saturday, a day after US President Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war in Ukraine. Three children were among those killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said on Saturday. At least 18 people were wounded in the attack. Missiles also struck Kyiv in a daytime...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
When 60,000 football fans gathered in Jeddah for the Arabian Gulf Cup on Tuesday, they inadvertently highlighted the vulnerability of major sports events hosted by Gulf monarchies to the wars raging across the region. The previous day, Saudi Arabia resumed strikes on Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi rebels after a four-year ceasefire collapsed. That truce had originally followed a Houthi attack on an oil facility near Jeddah’s Formula One track during a practice session. While the two-week football...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: How Taiwan’s military manpower shortage is undermining its ability to fight.
Taiwan’s military is grappling with a worsening manpower shortage, with its volunteer staffing rate remaining below the 80 per cent target for a third consecutive year and concerns mounting over the impact on combat readiness, according to the island’s legislature. The shortages extend deep into frontline formations – including infantry, artillery, missile and air defence units – raising questions over whether Taiwan will have enough trained personnel to operate and maintain the vast quantities...
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Spirit of Hong Kong Awards: Gaza nurse’s obstacle-laden road to becoming a professor.
On six occasions, Hammoda Abu-Odah, a Gaza nurse-turned Hong Kong scholar was offered an opportunity to study overseas. But each time, border closures and travel restrictions prevented him from taking them up. Abu-Odah had obtained a nursing degree in his native Gaza but set his sights on an academic career abroad. He kept working, teaching and conducting research, despite the many challenges that prevented him from leaving. Finally, on the seventh attempt, he made it to Hong Kong, where he...
India - bottom line: How A Series Of Mistakes Pulled Saudi Arabia Back Into Yemen War.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: How A Series Of Mistakes Pulled Saudi Arabia Back Into Yemen War.
Missiles and drones from Iran-backed Houthis have hit Saudi cities and oil facilities in recent weeks.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Poland holds emergency meeting over possible attack on PM Tusk, defence minister.
Polish security services convened an emergency meeting following a reported threat against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Authorities have been on high alert due to recent violent incidents at schools in Poland. These incidents led to arrests and concerns about online glorification of violence among youth. Tusk emphasized the spontaneous nature of these acts, suggesting no organized group is involved.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: ‘Going home to be with family as my grandmother has passed away’: Dipke.
Ahead of a significant protest, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, was detained while rallying for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities. Police claimed he was made aware of his grandmother’s demise, but family discussions reveal inconsistencies. Dipke intends to return home for family support during this tough time, while his party leaders prepare for a press conference on their next steps.
